newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet postpones meeting at govt.
newsitem.headline: Eramet postpones meeting at govt.

text.p: Eramet had cancelled its annual general meeting due on May 29 amid deteriorating relations with its main shareholder state holding Erap.
Erap, which controls 55 percent of Eramet, has threatened to take control of Eramet's board and to oust chairman Yves Rambaud, who opposes any plans to curb the group's expansion in New Caledonia.

The previous conservative government backed a plan by local Kanak company Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) to build a nickel plant in the north of the French territory with Canadian group Falconbridge, using nickel from Eramet's Koniambo mine.

In exchange Eramet would gain access to SMSP's Poum mine but Eramet and minority shareholders have said they must be compensated for the exchange. The state supports the plan to appease Kanak separatists ahead of a 1998 referendum on independence.

Besides Erap's proposal to oust Rambaud, board members were due to review on June 24 proposals put forward by minority investors aimed at insuring the independence of the future board. Staff representatives also wanted employees to be given the chance to select three directors under a 1983 public sector law.
The Socialist government has not yet revealed its intentions on the politically-sensitive issue of the New Caledonian smelter, nor on the fate of Rambaud.
The spokesman said that negotiations over the transfer of mining assets in New Caledonia were currently on hold, possibly until the state discloses its position.
The last round of talks between the mining experts of Eramet and SMSP was held in early June in Noumea, he said.
The third largest nickel producer in the world, Eramet plans to expand nickel output in New Caledonia to 60,000-65,0000 tonnes from the year 2000 from a current 54,000 tonnes.
